scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jumpstyle originated in Belgium in the late 1990s, around 1997–1998, with early contributions from artists like Da Boy Tommy.
It developed further in the Netherlands and Germany in the early 2000s.
The genre peaked commercially between 2006 and 2008, with hits by Jeckyll & Hyde and Scooter's international success.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Jumpstyle is danced socially at clubs, festivals, and competitions.
It is a non-sacred, secular dance form associated with electronic music culture.
Competitions occur both online and in person, including European Jump Masters and World Sidejump League.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Jumpstyle dance, called jumpen, involves energetic jumps, fast kicks, and rotational footwork timed to the music.
Dancers keep a stiff upper body and focus movement in their legs.

Variants include oldschool (simple 5-touch steps), hardjump (6-touch steps with faster tempo), sidejump (more rotations, less popular), hardfreestyle (blend of hardjump and sidejump), and ownstyle (innovative, incorporating spins and influences from hip-hop and ballet).
Watch for Basic 5-touch step, Spin, Duo-kick.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Jumpstyle music features tempos between 140 and 160 BPM, a four-on-the-floor 909 kick drum rhythm, and melodic elements from hardstyle such as pitched basslines and square wave synthesizers.
It developed from tech-trance, hardstyle, gabber, and makina.
Listen for the 909 kick drum, synthesizers with square waveforms, basslines, multiband distortion effects.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 140 beats a minute.

Jumpstyle music features a steady, driving four-on-the-floor 909 kick drum at 140–160 BPM, layered with pitched basslines and square wave synthesizers. The sound is minimal yet energetic, with rhythmic offbeats and melodic elements drawn from hardstyle and techno hardcore.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Patrick Jumpen is a seminal figure in jumpstyle dance and music, known for popularizing the dance and producing tutorials.
DJs and producers like Da Boy Tommy, Jeckyll & Hyde, Scooter, and Lithuanian rapper Yabujin have been influential in the music scene.
Variants of jumpstyle dance include oldschool, hardjump, sidejump, hardfreestyle, ownstyle, and tekstyle.
Jumpstyle descends from European hard dance genres such as gabber, hardstyle, tech-trance, and makina, with early influences from Chicago hard house.

Jumpstyle is parent of hardstyle: Incorporates melodic and bassline features from hardstyle.
Jumpstyle is parent of tech-trance: Early influence on jumpstyle's sound.
Jumpstyle is parent of makina: Contributed to jumpstyle's early development in Europe.
